rules.name: Win never the favorite
rules.description: Win bet is never the chalk. We find value — the fav goes in exotics only.

rules.name: Win must be 7/2+
rules.description: Win bet must be at least 7/2 odds. If our pick moves below that, pivot.

rules.name: Trifecta minimum 4 horses
rules.description: No 3-horse tri boxes (0/6 day one). Need width — 4 or 5 horse boxes.

rules.name: Fav always in exotics
rules.description: The favorite is always included in exacta and trifecta — they hit the board too often to exclude.

rules.name: Scratches require full rebuild
rules.description: Don't just remove — re-evaluate pace, bias, and who benefits from the scratch.

rules.name: Tri must include exacta horses
rules.description: Trifecta box ALWAYS contains the same horses as the exacta box. Never split them. (Added 5/30 — Mike's Mistake)

signals.name: Elite jockey on bomb
signals.description: Top-3 meet rider chooses a >12/1 horse over shorter-priced mounts. They know something.

signals.name: Late tote action
signals.description: Horse drops 3+ points from ML by post time. Sharp money = information.

signals.name: Odds drift on quality
signals.description: Was fav or co-fav on ML, now drifted to 4/1+. Form didn't change, just money flow. Gift.

signals.name: Hot barn at a price
signals.description: Trainer win% >15% at meet running a horse at >6/1. Barn cashing regardless of perception.

signals.name: Distance stretch to sire sweet spot
signals.description: Horse getting their sire's optimal distance for the first time. Pedigree unlocking.

signals.name: Best Beyer in field
signals.description: Highest speed figure among live starters. Proven fastest horse in here.

signals.name: Blinkers change
signals.description: Trainer making an equipment move = intent. Something different today.

signals.name: Track bias alignment
signals.description: Horse's running style (speed/stalker/closer) matches today's track pattern.

signals.name: Earnings leader in class
signals.description: Most $ earned among starters at this class level. Proven they belong.

signals.name: First-timer + expensive pedigree
signals.description: FTS with $100K+ stud fee or purchase price. Connections paid up and expect a run.

signals.name: Good jockey / good trainer on bad horse
signals.description: Top connections on a horse the public has dismissed. They see something the market doesn't.

win.name: Moroder
win.reason: Elite jockey Ortiz Jr (27% meet win rate) on a horse with back-to-back wins and strong dirt form (8-2-1-1). Highest value at a price among non-favorites at 7/2+. Beyer 74 is competitive in this field and the hot form off Turfway victories gives him the edge over weaker longshots.

0.notes: If #1 Moroder moves to favoritism or drifts below 7/2, pivot win bet to #6 League Of Legends at 6/1 as the only remaining 7/2+ option with any form. If #4 Shadow Coast scratches, rebuild entirely around pace dynamics.
0.analysis: This is a competitive $20K claimer at 6 furlongs with the favorite Shadow Coast (#4) holding the highest Beyer (75) and proven CD form, making him a must-use in exotics. The pace should be honest with multiple speed types, favoring horses that can press or stalk. Our win bet targets value: Moroder (#1) brings elite connections (Ortiz Jr) and red-hot form (back-to-back Turfway wins) at 4/1, satisfying the 7/2+ requirement while the favorite is eliminated. Aerate (#2) gets Asmussen's 17% barn and already won at CD this meet at 7f, making her dangerous at any trip. The exacta captures the three horses with the best combination of form, class, and connections. The trifecta adds League Of Legends (#6) for required width despite being an 8-year-old with fading form—necessary to satisfy the 4-horse minimum. Note that Homie (#3) is dismissed entirely due to 0-for-0 dirt fast record and first-time CD surface switch, while Gallo De Fuego (#5) is ignored for being 0-for-6 on dirt fast despite the Into Mischief pedigree.

win.name: Galatina
win.reason: Hot barn signal fires (Asmussen 16% at meet), elite Hall of Fame trainer, second-highest earnings ($73K) proves class level, and 6/1 odds provide value. Asmussen barns cashing at this rate require respect regardless of inconsistent individual record.

1.notes: If #5 Galatina moves under 7/2 by post, pivot win bet to #7 State Charmer (10/1, elite jockey Saez). Favorite #1 must stay in all exotics per Rule R4.
1.analysis: This is a wide-open $30K claimer where form is unreliable but connections matter. The favorite Quinn's Promise is most proven but offers no value at 9/5. The real story is Don't Be Salty (#3) - Ortiz Jr taking the call with first-time blinkers for Sharp's hot barn (16%) and carrying the best speed figure. At 3/1 this horse can't be the win bet but anchors the exotics. Galatina gets the win call because Asmussen's 16% meet win rate is a hard signal - when this barn fires at that clip, you back them at 6/1 regardless of the 1-for-13 record. The trifecta adds State Charmer because Saez at 10/1 on a young, improving horse (50% ITM from limited starts) fits our 'elite jockey sees something' profile. Pace should set up for stalkers with multiple speed types contesting early.

win.name: Whiskey Shot
win.reason: Whiskey Shot fires on B6 (best Beyer 75 in field) and B9 (earnings leader at $81K). Asmussen hot barn (16%) running a lightly-raced Gun Runner colt with room to improve. At 9/2, he's the highest-quality horse at a legitimate price - proven speed figures and class above this level.

2.notes: If Whiskey Shot moves below 3/1 by post time, pivot win bet to #1 Hardtoblame (8/1, Asmussen hot barn). Watch for late money on #6 Il Cavallino - he's never won in 6 tries but hits the board consistently.
2.analysis: Pace should be moderate with Fast Joker (#2) and the favorite Il Cavallino (#6) likely pressing early. This sets up well for Whiskey Shot's stalking style. Class-wise, this is the perfect spot for #4 - he's earned $81K lifetime which is 50% more than any other runner, and his Beyer 75 is the highest in the field. He's dropping from tougher spots and gets the Asmussen barn firing at 16%. The favorite #6 has never won (0-for-6) but places consistently, so he's a must-use in exotics. Stefan's Title (#3) gets Ortiz JL at 4/1, and Hardtoblame (#1) adds Asmussen depth at 8/1 for the trifecta. Gun Runner progeny (Whiskey Shot's sire) excel with pace to chase, and this race sets up perfectly for that. Best value is our win bet at 9/2 on the class of the field.

win.name: Sawyer Fox
win.reason: Best form in the field with 33% lifetime win rate and $109K earnings. Consistent at this claiming level with proven ability to close the deal. Value play at 10/1 against a weak favorite showing only a 75 Beyer.

3.notes: If #5 moves below 7/2, pivot win bet to #6 Raising Kane (12/1, Asmussen barn). If #2 scratches, rebuild entire race - favorite removal changes pace dynamics.
3.analysis: Wide-open $16K claimer at 6F where class and consistency matter most. #2 Lord Majesty is a vulnerable favorite with the lowest Beyer (75) among contenders. #8 Top Gun Tommy brings a monster 94 Beyer and $495K in lifetime earnings - the proven commodity stepping down. #5 Sawyer Fox shows best win percentage (33%) and represents value at 10/1 against a soft favorite. #7 Bebedouro adds Gaffalione (elite meet rider) on a Sharp barn firing at 16% - can't leave that combo out of the tri in a claimer where any horse can hit the board. Pace likely competitive with multiple speed types in a sprint, favoring horses who can settle and finish. The win bet targets form and value; the exotics cover the favorite, the speed standout, and elite connections.

win.name: Admiral Hall
win.reason: Elite connections with Gaffalione and hot trainer Jacobson, best Beyer in field (76), War Front pedigree, lightly raced with room to improve. Qualifies at exactly 7/2 and represents best value over the overbet favorite.

4.notes: If #3 Admiral Hall moves below 7/2 to favoritism, pivot win bet to #5 Truly Legit at 4/1 (second-best Beyer, Into Mischief pedigree for distance).
4.analysis: Small 5-horse starter allowance with limited pace pressure. Favorite #1 Baytown Bruiser is overbet at 9/5 given pedestrian record (2-for-23) despite highest earnings. Admiral Hall at 7/2 is the value play combining elite jockey Gaffalione with hot trainer Jacobson (explicitly noted), best available Beyer (76), and upside from limited experience (only 3 starts). War Front pedigree adds class. Truly Legit offers secondary value at 4/1 with Authentic/Into Mischief line suited to the mile and second-best Beyer (71). Exacta covers the favorite (likely to hit board in small field) plus top two value plays. Trifecta adds You Ain't Poppn at 6/1 for required 4-horse width based on decent 33% win rate. Signal scoring low across field - this race decided by class, connections, and form rather than explosive pattern signals.

win.name: Vino Dominus
win.reason: Vino Dominus has the best resume in this field: 2 wins from 7 starts, highest Beyer figure (70), and highest earnings ($27K). Signals B6 (best Beyer) and B9 (earnings leader) both fire here. At 9/2, we're getting value on a horse that should be closer to favoritism based on proven form and speed figures. The only horse with multiple wins and the experience edge over this weak maiden claiming field.

5.notes: If #9 Vino Dominus moves to favoritism (shorter than #1 Carson), pivot win bet to #5 Paired (8/1) on the hot trainer angle. Jacobson is noted as a hot trainer and Paired shows the highest speed rating despite being 0-for-3. If both #9 and #5 drift to co-favoritism, pivot to #10 Tims (6/1) - 3 wins and proven form.
5.analysis: This is a weak maiden claiming field where only two horses have multiple wins: Vino Dominus (2) and Tims (3). The pace sets up with limited early speed, likely making this a tactical race where class and speed figures matter more than running style. Carson is the ML favorite at 7/2 despite never winning - presumably on recent form or workouts not shown in the PPs. Vino Dominus presents clear value at 9/2 with the highest Beyer (70 vs field average around 50), proven winning ability, and highest earnings. Paired gets into the exotics on the hot trainer signal (Jacobson noted) and the highest speed rating note - at 8/1 with only 3 career starts, there's upside if the barn thinks they're ready. Tims rounds out the trifecta with 3 wins and $26K banked. The favorite Carson must be included per strategy rules despite the thinner resume. This exacta and tri structure captures the proven form horses (9, 10) while including the improving angle (5) and the public's choice (1).

win.name: Secret Hideaway
win.reason: Fires six signals - highest in field. Beyer 71 best figure by far. First-time blinkers from Walsh (16% barn) signals intent. Gaffalione (elite) + Walsh (elite) on dismissed 8/1 horse triggers B11 - they see something the public doesn't.

6.notes: If #8 moves below 7/2, pivot win bet to #7 Mony Mony at 4/1. Favorite #1 Beach Heist must stay in all exotics per Rule R4.
6.analysis: Short turf sprint for 3YO fillies. Beach Heist is the rightful favorite with Prat and a 30% combo, but Rule R1 forces us to find value elsewhere. Secret Hideaway is that value - her six triggered signals are the most in the field, led by the equipment change (first-time blinkers from a 16% barn) and best Beyer figure (71 vs next-best 24). The B11 signal captures the key insight: Gaffalione and Walsh are both elite, yet this horse is 8/1. They don't waste mounts or equipment moves. Mony Mony is the earnings leader ($197K) with Ortiz Jr aboard and the highest speed rating - she's getting proper respect at 4/1. Sapphire Beach (5/2) rounds out the trifecta with consistent form (4 of 6 ITM) and Ortiz JL. The exacta box captures the favorite, our value play, and the class horse. Trifecta adds the second choice for coverage.

win.name: Delancey Street
win.reason: Highest signal score at 5 points. Gaffalione/Casse are elite connections that don't waste FTS entries — both B1 and B11 fired. Street Sense sire can get 6.5f. At 12/1 this is exceptional value for a horse that could easily be 6/1 or 7/2 based on connections alone.

7.notes: If #8 takes heavy late money and drops below 7/1, pivot win bet to #9 Gadget Play (Into Mischief $250K with Saez at 8/1). If #11 scratches, rebuild entirely — the favorite scratch changes the whole dynamic.
7.analysis: This maiden sprint sets up as a debut-horse lottery, but the connections tell the story. Campobasso (Prat/Baffert) is rightfully favored at 4/1 and must be in all exotics. Study (McCarthy hot trainer) at 5/1 is the logical second choice. But the value play is Delancey Street at 12/1 — Gaffalione and Casse on an FTS is a 'good jockey/good trainer on bad odds' situation. They chose this horse, they entered it here, and the public is dismissing it. Gadget Play adds exotic depth with his $250K Into Mischief pedigree and Saez, while Civic Charm (Mott) gives us another proven barn at a price. Five-horse trifecta provides the width Rule R3 demands after the 3-horse box failures on day one.
